root_cause.text: The Iris media driver’s `sm8750_data` platform descriptor was missing SM8750-specific capability and buffer-sizing callbacks, so the VPU33 buffer allocation path and encoder capability limits were never configured for that SoC.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `get_vpu_buffer_size = iris_vpu33_buf_size` to `sm8750_data`, and the commit message says that without it “the driver fails to allocate the required internal buffers, leading to basic decode/encode failures during session bring-up”; it also adds `max_core_mbps = ((7680 * 4320) / 256) * 60`, noting that without this field “capability checks are incomplete and v4l2-compliance for encoder fails.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the SM8750 VPU buffer size callback so the platform uses the correct buffer sizing logic.
intent_record.what: A new platform data field assignment was added to `sm8750_data`: `.get_vpu_buffer_size = iris_vpu33_buf_size,` placed before the existing `.vpu_ops = &iris_vpu35_ops,` entry.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the SM8750 platform will now use `iris_vpu33_buf_size` to determine the VPU buffer size instead of relying on whatever default or previously inherited behavior existed, which can affect memory allocation and VPU setup for this platform.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing SM8750 core throughput limit definition.
intent_record.what: A new initializer entry, `max_core_mbps`, was added to `sm8750_data` and set to `((7680 * 4320) / 256) * 60`.
intent_record.how: This provides the SM8750 platform with an explicit maximum core megapixels-per-second value, allowing code that consults this limit to use a defined throughput cap instead of lacking one.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by adding the missing SM8750-specific VPU buffer sizing callback to the platform descriptor, which is part of the misconfiguration that left buffer allocation logic unconfigured.

The root cause is that the SM8750 platform descriptor lacked SM8750-specific capability/buffer-sizing configuration. Adding the missing SM8750 core throughput limit is part of supplying the SoC-specific encoder capability limits, so this change directly relates to the vulnerable missing configuration.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix platform descriptor uses the generic VPU ops without an SM8750-specific buffer sizing callback, which directly matches the root cause that the VPU33 buffer allocation path was never configured for SM8750.

The SM8750 descriptor was still reusing SM8550 configuration-only hooks and lacked its own platform-specific callback set, indicating the missing SM8750-specific capability/buffer configuration described in the root cause.
This line encodes the core throughput limit for the platform; before the fix, SM8750 had no dedicated throughput limit definition, which can leave encoder capability limits incorrectly configured.
This pre-fix configuration block shows the platform inheriting default input-config parameters rather than an SM8750-specific setup, consistent with missing SM8750 capability configuration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This platform descriptor used the generic VPU35 ops instead of an SM8750-specific ops set, so the SM8750 buffer sizing callback was not configured. That matches the root cause that the VPU33 buffer allocation path was never set up for SM8750.
This is the core throughput limit field for the platform. Before the fix, SM8750 lacked its dedicated capability limit definition, which could leave encoder capability limits incorrectly configured.

Author: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzk@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Sep 2 14:45:12 2025 +0200

    media: iris: Add support for SM8750 (VPU v3.5)
    
    Add support for SM8750 Iris codec with major differences against
    previous generation SM8650:
    
    1. New clocks and new resets, thus new power up and power down
       sequences,
    
    2. New WRAPPER_IRIS_VCODEC_VPU_WRAPPER_SPARE_0 register programmed
       during boot-up
    
    Signed-off-by
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient to determine whether the SM8750 platform descriptor now includes the missing configuration. The new `sm8750_data` structure explicitly adds the SM8750-specific callbacks and tables relevant to the root cause: `.vpu_ops = &iris_vpu35_ops`, `.clk_rst_tbl = sm8750_clk_reset_table`, `.clk_tbl = sm8750_clk_table`, and the buffer/capability tables such as `.inst_caps = &platform_inst_cap_sm8550`, `.inst_fw_caps = inst_fw_cap_sm8550`, `.dec_ip_int_buf_tbl = sm8550_dec_ip_int_buf_tbl`, and `.dec_op_int_buf_tbl = sm8550_dec_op_int_buf_tbl`. Since the root cause was that SM8750 was missing capability and buffer-sizing callbacks, and this snippet shows those platform descriptor fields are now present, the vulnerable construct is not present here. Therefore `has_bug` is NO and `is_fixed` is YES.
